hints: Notice how much the newton meter reading falls from $W$ to $P$ in water and from $W$ to $Q$ in oil - each fall equals the upthrust in that liquid.
Recall Archimedes principle: upthrust $= \rho V g$, where $V$ is the volume of the completely immersed object, the same in water and in oil.
Write $W-P = \rho_{water}Vg$ and $W-Q = \rho_{oil}Vg$, then divide the oil equation by the water equation to cancel $Vg$.
walkthrough: The object has true weight $W$ in air. When suspended in a fluid the meter reads less because upthrust acts upward, so upthrust $=$ $W$ $-$ meter reading.
In water the reading is $P$, so upthrust in water $U_{water} = W-P$. In oil the reading is $Q$, so upthrust in oil $U_{oil} = W-Q$.
By Archimedes principle, $U = \rho V g$ where $\rho$ is fluid density and $V$ is displaced volume. The object is completely immersed in both cases so $V$ is identical.
Divide to find the density ratio: $\frac{\rho_{oil}}{\rho_{water}} = \frac{(W-Q)/Vg}{(W-P)/Vg} = \frac{W-Q}{W-P}$.

A.explanation: This inverts the fluids by putting $W-P$ for water on top and uses $Q-P$ which is only the difference between the two readings, not an upthrust.

B.explanation: The numerator $Q-P$ is the difference between the oil and water readings, not the upthrust $W-Q$ in oil.

C.explanation: This is the inverse ratio, density of water divided by density of oil, since $W-P$ is the upthrust in water and $W-Q$ is the upthrust in oil.

D.explanation: Upthrust in oil is $W-Q$ and in water is $W-P$, so their ratio equals the density ratio because $V$ and $g$ cancel.
